thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Original thesis: strong brands, operating underperformance, potential for improved capital efficiency [D01].

Current status: Management has adopted some measures such as a margin objective and buyback, but performance continues to fall short of expectations, indicating further need for structural change [D03].
Evidence: Fourth-quarter organic growth slowed to 1.9%, and headline results remain pressured by decentralization [D02, D03].
final.remaining_skew: Significant upside potential remains by closing the margin gap versus peers and optimizing the portfolio, vs limited downside protected by strong brands [D01, D06].
final.next_catalyst_and_timing: Public presentation 'NestléNOW' (published today, 2018-07-01) provides the basis for an accelerated shift in portfolio and operational strategy [D01, D03].
asks_if_escalating: Accelerate margin expansion toward the 17.5-18.5% target
Optimize portfolio composition to address the underperforming long tail of categories
Drive more aggressive capital allocation and operational discipline

drivers.driver: Persistent organic growth deceleration with fourth-quarter growth down to 1.9% [D02].
Operating margins continue to lag behind category peers despite some management efforts [D03, D06].
The complexity of the current decentralized structure continues to obscure the underlying value of the core business [D01].
Opportunity to amplify the case for change following today's 'NestléNOW' presentation [D01].

final.memo:
Nestlé remains a collection of high-quality assets buried beneath a legacy of decentralization and bureaucratic inertia. While CEO Schneider has taken initial steps toward a buyback and margin targets, these are modest improvements rather than the structural transformation this company requires [D03]. Our engagement has reached a stage where private suggestions are no longer sufficient to drive the urgency needed in a global group facing slowing organic growth [D03, D05].

Today, we publish 'NestléNOW' to highlight the clear margin gap vs. best-in-class peers and to demand a more aggressive approach to portfolio simplification [D01, D06]. The company has the brands to be a top-tier performer, but the current structure continues to fail to convert that customer value into sustainable cash for owners [D01]. We are not content to wait for slow-motion recovery when the levers for value creation—portfolio rationalization and operational sharpening—are visible and underutilized [D05].

Our decision to escalate is a direct response to the persistence of the mispricing and the inadequacy of the current pace of execution [D03, D05]. We expect management to move beyond the current plan and demonstrate a commitment to shareholder returns that matches the caliber of the franchise [D03].
